newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to propose rules for children's drug labels.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to propose rules for children's drug labels.

text.p: President Clinton plans to propose Wednesday that drug companies be required to put dosage information on labels for children's drugs, a senior White House official said Tuesday.

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Clinton planned to stage a White House event to announce the proposed regulations, which would allow the Health and Human Services Department to require dosage information to be given for children's drugs in both prescription and over-the-counter varieties.
Many drug labels offer no dosage information for children, saying simply that parents should consult their physicians. Adult medicines offer precise dosage information.

HHS Secretary Donna Shalala, talking to reporters aboard Air Force One on Clinton's flight to Washington from a day trip to St. Louis, said Clinton's wife, Hillary, has been particularly concerned about the absence of dosage information on children's drug containers.
"Children are not little adults" when it comes to determining the dose of medicine they should take for an illness, she said.
Without commenting on the details of the initiative, she said Clinton's announcement would be "something all parents will be able to relate to."
Shalala said the initiative would probably require drug companies to conduct tests of medicines to determine proper dosages for children.
